result.title: Realism VS Accuracy: Event Sequence Forecasting from a Generative Modeling Perspective
result.comment: Spotlight at the NeurIPS 2026 Track on Evaluations and Datasets. Code: https://github.com/xaosina/event-sequence-forecasting
result.summary: Event sequences are chains of random events, each described by heterogeneous (numerical and categorical) features. The problem of event sequence forecasting occurs in finance, healthcare, business process intelligence, and other fields. In this work, we study multi-horizon forecasting of event sequences as a conditional generative modeling problem. We evaluate forecasts not only for prediction accuracy, but also for distributional realism. To this end, we present a benchmark comprising metrics for both quality aspects, strong statistical baselines, recent models adapted from adjacent fields, and curated real-world datasets. Careful evaluation reveals that no method excels at both accuracy and realism, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between the two. Finally, we introduce Wasserstein BaryBooster, an algorithm that aggregates samples from a realism-strong diffusion model into a state-of-the-art predictor, demonstrating that distributional realism can be converted into prediction accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/xaosina/event-sequence-forecasting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把事件序列的多步预测建模为条件生成任务，提出同时衡量准确率与分布真实性的基准，发现两者存在权衡，并提出 Wasserstein BaryBooster 把强真实性的扩散模型样本聚合进判别式预测器以换取准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多样性/真实性样本经 Wasserstein 重心聚合为单点预测」的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中多条 latent 推理轨迹的聚合、筛选与多样性—准确率取舍问题。
